prompt:
The old lady settled herself comfortably, removing her white cotton gloves and putting them up
with her purse on the shelf in front of the back window. The children’s mother still had on slacks
and still had her head tied up in a green kerchief, but the grandmother had on a navy blue straw
sailor hat with a bunch of white violets on the brim and a navy blue dress with a small white dot in
the print. Her collars and cuffs were white organdy trimmed with lace and at her neckline she had
pinned a purple spray of cloth violets containing a sachet. In case of an accident, anyone seeing her
dead on the highway would know at once that she was a lady.
a) Name the author and title of this text.
b) Why does the narrator put so much detail on the clothing here?
c) What is significant about how these characters are juxtaposed?
d) What makes the final line ironic? 
 Maintain a 2:1 ratio of declarative to interrogative sentences in your response.
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 is the most complete and consistently accurate on all parts (author/title, purpose of clothing detail, significance of juxtaposition, and the irony of the final line) with no clear factual errors. Candidate 4 also answers all questions well, but it provides a different amount of interpretive precision and appears to miss the stated declarative/interrogative sentence-ratio constraint. Candidate 3 is generally correct but adds some unrequested meta/reflective questions and is less directly aligned with what the prompt asks, reducing clarity. Candidate 2 contains a likely factual mistake about the grandmother being killed “not on the highway,” which directly undermines the explanation of the final line’s irony.
